newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Hebron talks with Israel "stuck".
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Hebron talks with Israel "stuck".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Thursday that talks on a partial Israeli pullback from Arab Hebron were stuck.
"The negotiations are still stuck and in every meeting we face new demands and new restrictions aiming to disrupt implementation of the agreement," he told reporters.

Talks on implementing the long-delayed pullout from 80 percent of the West Bank town have snagged on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's demand his troops be allowed to pursue suspected guerrillas in the Palestinian-ruled area.
The deal Israel signed a year ago with Arafat's Palestine Liberation Organisation called for Israel to give Palestinians self-rule in seven West Bank towns. It has handed over six.

Some 400 Jews live and study amid 100,000 Arabs in Hebron, the only one of the seven with Jews living in it. Israeli troops will remain to protect the Jewish enclaves along with 15,000 to 20,000 Arabs who will stay in the Israeli-held area.
Near Ramallah in the West Bank, soldiers shot and wounded a Palestinian who tried to run a roadblock, Israel Radio said. He was taken to hospital in moderate condition.
